answer: Keep two specimens, not one. E19 Physical Object's own scope note requires 'physical boundaries that separate them completely in an objective way from other objects' -- the two core segments sit in separate boxes in separate buildings and never touch, so each stays its own E19 Physical Object instance no matter what the strata once looked like underground. Each keeps the P1/P48 identifier (accession number) it was given by its own crew's E15 Identifier Assignment; per the Monotonicity principle (new insight must not retract previously correct statements), the fifty years of loan paperwork that cites those two numbers stays valid as-is and does not need to be rewritten or merged. The newly recognised fact -- that the segments were once continuous rock -- is added as a new assertion, not a retroactive identity change: document it with P46 is composed of/forms part of, treating both segments as parts of the single original rock body they were extracted from (this is the same whole-part pattern CRM uses for a carriage forming part of a train, or, per Issue 720's discomfort with over-literal P46 examples, one that should be used carefully). Because this is an expert's interpretation of old logs rather than a directly observed fact, the stratigrapher's reasoning itself is better carried by CRMinf: an I5 Inference Making activity (premises: the two old core logs) concluding an I2 Belief that the P46 relation holds -- exactly the path the SIG pointed to when it closed Issue 544 (CRMtex Fragment Ordering) by ruling that reconstructing a physical whole from separately catalogued fragments -- sherds, statues, papyri, jigsaws -- is 'not much different' a reasoning problem and belongs in CRMinf rather than as a bespoke class or a silent merge.

rejected_alternatives.option: Merge into a single E19 instance
rejected_alternatives.why_not: E19's scope note defines the class by objective, complete physical boundary separation from other objects; the two segments are discrete pieces of matter in different repository buildings, so they fail that criterion even though the rock they came from was once continuous. Merging would also silently override two independently-assigned, still-cited accession identifiers, which the Monotonicity principle (docs, Modelling principles > Monotonicity) says correct existing statements should not have to retract.

Appears as a candidate link between two E19/S22 instances via `connect`, but its own scope note calls it 'a non-unique identification' and it is a CRMdig property built for record co-reference/deduplication of digital surrogates, not a claim of material identity between physical specimens.

Its scope note explicitly lists 'earthquake induced faults' as an example physical-relation type, which felt close, but its domain/range is A8 Stratigraphic Unit -- an in-situ excavation-interpretation class -- not curated, accessioned museum/repository specimens with their own loan history.

rejected_alternatives.option: CRMsci S22 Segment of Matter for the extracted cores themselves
rejected_alternatives.why_not: S22's scope note (matter with declared, sometimes-unobserved boundaries, subsections continuing to exist as segments 'in their own right') describes the in-situ geological layer well, but once drilled out and boxed the cores are discrete, individually catalogued specimens -- E19's 'unit for documentation' framing fits the accessioned object better than S22's continuous-matter framing.
